Thanks for installing Makullveny.

Makullveny is a study app for students. It is made by two people, not a company, and this agreement is written to be read rather than skimmed past. It is the agreement between you and us about using the app.

It is the same text as Part A of the LICENSE file that ships with the app. That file has a second part, about the source code, which applies only to people we have given access to it — there is nothing in it you need in order to use Makullveny.

Definitions: "the app" is Makullveny, including its installers, updates, artwork, audio, text, and the services it talks to. "we", "us" and "our" are Nate McIlvenny and Luke McIlvenny. "you" is the person using it. "your work" is what you write, draw, import, and organise inside it.

By clicking "I Agree" and installing the app, you accept these terms. If you do not accept them, close this installer.

A1. Agreeing to this

Installing, opening, or using the app means you accept these terms. If you do not accept them, do not install it, and delete any copy you have.

If we have given you a pre-release, beta, or play-test build, section A15 also applies to you, and it matters.

A2. Who may use it

a. You must be at least 13 years old. The app is not offered to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect anything from them. If you learn that a child under 13 has an account, tell us and we will remove it.

b. If you are under 18, you may use the app only with the knowledge and permission of a parent or guardian, and they accept these terms with you.

c. A school, district, or organisation that wants to deploy the app to students needs a separate written agreement with us. These terms cover one person using it for themselves.

d. AGE CHECKS. Some app stores, including Apple's, can tell an app which age range a person is in, or ask a parent to approve a change. Where that is offered, the app may use the answer to decide which features fit your age — for example, whether friends and Study Teams are on by default. We use that answer for nothing else.

A3. What you may do

We give you a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to:

a. install and run the app on devices you own or personally control, for your own studying and your own work; b. keep your own backups of your own installation and your own data; c. use every feature your account is entitled to (see A10).

That is a license to USE the app. Nothing in it transfers ownership of the app, and nothing in it is a sale of the software itself.

A4. What stays ours

a. The app, its code, design, artwork, sprites, audio, icons, written copy, the Selah world, and the name "Makullveny" are ours, or are used by us under license from someone else.

b. This document grants no rights to the TDG name, the Makullveny name, or any logo or mark. No patent license is granted.

c. Anything not expressly granted here stays with us.

A5. Your work is yours

a. Your notes, books, pages, drawings, quick notes, flashcards, classes, imported files, and everything else you make in the app belong to you. We claim no ownership of any of it and no license to it, with the one narrow exception in A13 for a page you deliberately choose to publish.

b. The app is local-first. By default your work is stored in files on your own computer, and stays there. We cannot read it.

c. Export and Restore exist so your work is never trapped: `prefs.json` export, import, and "Restore latest backup" are part of the product and are not features we will take away.

d. If your account ends for any reason, your local files are unaffected. They are yours and they are on your machine.

A6. What leaves your computer, and when

Everything in this section is off unless you turn it on, with one exception: the basic usage counts in (g), which a signed-in account sends unless you switch them off. This is a plain summary and is meant to be accurate; where a feature has its own explanation inside the app, that explanation and this section are supposed to agree, and if they ever disagree, tell us, because one of them is a bug.

a. NOTHING BY DEFAULT. A fresh install with no account signed in sends us nothing about you and uploads none of your work.

b. A TDG ACCOUNT (optional). Signing in creates or uses a TDG account, which is shared across TDG's apps. It carries your sign-in details, your username, a display name and a picture if you set them, a short bio if you write one, your timezone if you let it, and which Makullveny features you have bought. It does not carry your writing.

c. CLOUD BACKPACK (optional, off by default). If you turn it on, the specific items you choose are copied to our server so you can get them back on another machine. You pick what goes in; nothing goes in on its own. There are size limits, and they are stated in the app.

d. CALENDAR FEEDS (optional). If you paste a calendar address from your school, the app fetches it so your classes and due dates appear. That address is treated as a credential: it is encrypted on your machine, never displayed back, and never included in an export or a backup.

e. PUBLIC LINK SHARING (optional). See A13. This one makes a page that anybody holding the link can open, so it is the one place where "your work stays on your computer" stops being true — and only for the exact page you chose.

f. THE TYPING LEADERBOARD (optional, off by default). If you opt in, your best typing score and your username are published on a board other people can see. You can delete your records.

g. USAGE COUNTS. Two kinds, and neither ever contains your work.

  1. BASIC COUNTS (signed-in accounts; on unless you switch them off). While you are signed in to a TDG account, the app sends a few numbers per day: how many times it was opened, how many minutes it was in use, which parts of it were used (for example Documents, Study Hall, Classes, Selah, the tools) and for how long, how many Lock Ins you started and finished and their focus minutes, the app's version, and whether your computer runs Windows, Mac or Linux. Signed out, nothing is sent. You can switch this off in Settings at any time, see exactly what the next send contains, and erase what was already sent. We keep these rows for at most 400 days.
  2. DETAILED COUNTS (optional, off by default). Only if you turn on "Help improve Makullveny", or press "Share a usage snapshot" after seeing what it holds, the daily numbers also include finer counts: which navigation buttons you used, which Lock In modes, how far the welcome tour got, and how many errors the app caught. We keep these finer counts for at most 90 days. Neither kind ever includes your notes, pages, drawings, book or class names, assignment names, file names, search terms, or anything you type. Only TDG can read them, and we look at them as totals and trends to see how the app is used and what to improve.

h. CLYDE (optional, per feature). Clyde is the in-app helper. It is opt-in for each module it can see, it does not watch your clipboard or your selections in the background, and as of this version there is no AI provider connected to it at all.

i. PAYMENTS. On a computer, Stripe processes the payment. On iPhone, Apple processes it through In-App Purchase, and a service called RevenueCat tells us what your purchase unlocks. We never see or store your card number. See A10.

j. CRASHES AND UPDATES. The app checks for updates. It does not upload your work to do it.

k. FRIENDS, STUDY TEAMS AND STUDY CALLS (optional). If you use them, the people you choose can see what those features show them: your profile (name, username, picture and bio), your status, the classes you choose to share, your Study Team's name and motto, and the study calls and waves you send. See A20.

l. EMAILS. A signed-in account gets a welcome email and a receipt when you buy something. News emails and the Lantern renewal reminder only come if you turn them on, and every email has a link to stop it.

The full detail — every kind of data, who helps us handle it, how long we keep it, and how to delete it — is in our Privacy Policy at makullveny.com/privacy/. It is part of these terms.

A7. Fair play

The app has things you can earn — focus streaks, coins and diamonds in Selah, achievements, a leaderboard — and things you can buy. Those are supposed to mean something, which means we have to say plainly what is not allowed:

a. Do not edit, patch, inject into, or replay the app, its saved files, its network traffic, or its server calls in order to give yourself coins, diamonds, achievements, leaderboard scores, themes, tiers, or any other entitlement you did not earn or buy.

b. Do not automate the app, run it under a bot or a script, or leave it running to farm rewards you are not present for. Time recorded as focus is supposed to be time you actually spent.

c. Do not use a bug to your advantage. If you find one, tell us — there is a Feedback door inside the app, and we would much rather hear about it. Finding a bug is not cheating; mining one is.

d. Do not attack, overload, probe, scrape, or try to gain unauthorised access to our servers, our database, our Edge Functions, or anybody else's account or data.

e. Do not attempt to bypass, disable, or defeat any licensing, entitlement, payment, or integrity check in the app.

f. Do not post anything — on a shared page, in a profile or bio, in a Study Team name or motto, in a study call, as a leaderboard name, or in a feedback message — that is unlawful, that infringes somebody's rights, that bullies, harasses, threatens or endangers a person, that is hateful or sexual, or that is sexual content involving minors. The Community Guidelines (A20) say the same thing in more detail.

Some of this is enforced by the software and by our servers; all of it is enforced by this agreement. Breaking A7 is the clearest way to lose your license under A17.

We say this once and mean it: reporting a security problem to us in good faith, without taking other people's data and without disrupting anybody else, is welcome and is not a breach of this agreement.

A8. Other things you must not do

a. Do not copy, publish, distribute, host, rent, lease, lend, sell, sublicense, or give away the app or any part of it. That includes uploading an installer anywhere, repackaging it, and putting it on a site for download.

b. Do not modify the app, or make anything derived from it, and do not remove or alter any notice, credit, or mark in it.

c. Do not reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble the app, or try to extract its source, assets, keys, or secrets from a build. This does not apply where, and only to the extent that, applicable law gives you a right that cannot be contracted away — if you are exercising such a right, please contact us first, because we would probably just tell you.

d. Do not use the app, its assets, its text, or its output as training, fine-tuning, evaluation, or benchmarking data for any machine-learning or AI system, and do not scrape it for that purpose.

e. Do not share your account, sell access to it, or use somebody else's.

f. Do not use the app to break the law, to infringe somebody's copyright, or to commit academic misconduct. The app is a place to do your work, not a way around doing it.

g. Do not use the app if you are barred from doing so by trade sanctions or export law that applies to you.

A9. Accounts

a. You are responsible for what happens under your account and for keeping your password to yourself.

b. We may suspend or end an account that breaks A7 or A8, that is being used to harm somebody, or that we are required to act on by law.

c. If we end your account for a reason other than a breach by you, and you have paid for something that is not delivered, contact us.

d. You can stop using the app at any time. Your local files stay yours and stay where they are.

e. DELETING. Signed in, Settings lets you delete in one of two ways, and you choose:

  1. "Delete my Makullveny data only" removes everything Makullveny keeps for your account on our server — your Cloud Backpack, synced classes and assignments, your Selah save, pictures, Study Teams you own, study calls, waves, reports you sent and usage counts — and turns off any link you made. Your TDG account and your friends list stay, so other TDG apps keep working, and a record of what you bought stays, so anything you paid for is still yours.
  2. "Delete my account from ALL TDG apps" deletes your TDG account itself, in every TDG app. It cannot be undone. If a paid plan is still renewing, cancel it first; the app tells you where.

Either way, the files on your own device stay where they are (A5d).

A10. Paying for things

a. WHAT IS FOR SALE TODAY. Makullveny is free to use. Some things are paid: a one-time "Candle" purchase, individual marketplace themes, and "Lantern", a monthly subscription. Prices are shown in the app before you buy. Features advertised but not yet built are not on sale, and the app is written to refuse to sell them.

b. WHAT A PURCHASE IS. Buying something gives you a license to use that feature or that theme under Part A. It is not a transfer of ownership and it is not a share of anything.

c. PAYMENT PROCESSING. On a computer, Stripe handles payment and Stripe's own terms apply to that part. On iPhone, Apple handles payment through In-App Purchase and Apple's own terms apply to that part. Your card details go to Stripe or Apple, never to us, and we never store them.

d. REFUNDS.

  1. Candle bought on a computer: you can ask for a full refund within 7 days of buying, for any reason, in Account > Payment history. After 7 days it is final. A full refund removes Candle. If you were charged twice by mistake, the extra charge is always refunded and Candle stays.
  2. Marketplace themes are final. You can try any theme for free before you buy it.
  3. Lantern: you can cancel at any time and keep it until the end of the month you paid for. We do not refund part of a month.
  4. Anything bought on iPhone is refunded by Apple, under Apple's rules, at reportaproblem.apple.com.

None of this takes away a refund right you have under the law where you live, or any refund your bank, card network, or a platform's own store policy makes us give.

e. TAXES are yours unless the law puts them on us.

f. PRICES CAN CHANGE. A change never reaches back: something you have already bought outright stays bought.

g. If a payment is reversed, charged back, or refunded, the entitlement it paid for can be removed.

h. SUBSCRIPTIONS. Lantern renews each month until you cancel it. Cancel on a computer in Account > Manage billing, or on iPhone in your Apple account's subscription settings. Deleting your account does not cancel an Apple subscription by itself: Apple keeps billing until you cancel it there.

A11. Coins, diamonds and anything else earned in the app

a. Coins, diamonds, streaks, achievements and items in Selah are part of a game inside a study app. They have NO cash value, are not money, are not a currency, are not securities, and are not property.

b. They cannot be bought with real money, sold, traded, transferred, cashed out, or redeemed for anything outside the app.

c. We may change, rebalance, or reset them as the game is built, and we may remove any that were obtained by breaking A7.

A12. The app is not a backup service

The app keeps local backups, and the Cloud Backpack keeps what you put in it. Neither is a promise. Keep your own copies of anything you cannot afford to lose. We are not liable for lost work (A16), and we would still rather it never happened — which is why Export exists and why it is not going away.

A13. Publishing a page

If you use public link sharing:

a. You keep ownership of what you publish. You give us only the narrow permission we need to host it, serve it to people with the link, and show it as you published it — nothing else, and only while it is published.

b. You must have the right to publish it. Do not publish somebody else's work, somebody else's private information, or anything covered by A7f.

c. A published page can be opened by anyone with the link. Treat it as public.

d. You can take it down at any time, and we can take one down if it breaks these terms or if we are required to. Readers can report a page.

e. If you believe a published page infringes your copyright, write to us with enough detail to identify the work and the page, and we will act on it.

A14. Other people's work inside the app

a. The app includes third-party software components. Each keeps its own license, and those licenses control for those components. They are listed in the app and in `docs/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

b. Scripture in the app is the World English Bible, which is in the public domain, and every verse is shown with its translation named. The short devotions are written for this app and are ours; they are not scripture, and the app says so on the card.

c. Fonts, sounds and images from other sources keep their own licenses.

A15. It is still being built

a. Makullveny is under active development, and some builds are given to a small number of people specifically to be tested.

b. A pre-release build may lose data, may change its saved format, may have features that do not work, and may be withdrawn. Do not keep anything in it that you have not backed up somewhere else.

c. If you are testing a pre-release build, please keep private anything we have not announced — screenshots, feature names, unreleased artwork — until we have. This is a request that carries weight, and we will say clearly when something is public.

d. Feedback you send us, and bug reports you make, may be used to improve the app without any obligation or payment to you. You keep the copyright in anything substantial you write; you give us permission to use it for that purpose.

A20. People you study with

a. Friends are by request: nobody becomes your friend unless you both agree. Study Teams are by invite or by code. There is no chat with strangers, no random or anonymous chat, and there will not be.

b. Be kind. The Community Guidelines at makullveny.com/community-guidelines/ are part of these terms.

c. REPORT. You can report a person, a bio, a Study Team, a study call or a wave from where you see it. What you report is hidden from you at once, and the person is never told who reported them. A real person at TDG reads every report, and we aim to act within 24 hours.

d. BLOCK. You can block anyone from the same places. A blocked person leaves your friends, the Study Teams you own, your study calls and your suggestions, and cannot wave to you.

e. Names, mottos, bios and study call messages are checked for words that are not allowed. A check like that is never perfect, which is why report and block exist.
